knowledge:
- key_parameters: profiles=Matrix of co-elution proteomics data with quantitations for each protein in each fraction ;; gold_standard=List of experimentally verified protein complexes used to train the classifier ;; gaussians=Pre-computed list of fitted Gaussians to save computation time ;; cv_folds=Number of folds to use in k-fold cross-validation ;; classifier=Type of classifier to use (NB, SVM, RF, LR, or ensemble) ;; models=Size of the ensemble for each classifier type ;; min_consecutive=Minimum number of consecutive points to retain a profile ;; min_R_squared=Minimum r2 value to retain the fitted curve ;; threshold=Precision threshold used to filter the predicted network
- alternatives: The permutation-based approach in detect_complexes is inspired by Thermal Proximity Co-Aggregation (TPCA) methods. For classification, users can choose between Naive Bayes (NB, default), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Logistic Regression (LR), or heterogeneous classifier fusion (ensemble).
- when_to_use: Use when reconstructing protein-protein interaction networks from co-elution, co-migration, co-fractionation, or protein correlation profiling proteomics data, or when testing whether known protein complexes show statistically significant co-elution.
- pitfalls: Fitting Gaussian mixture models is highly computationally intensive; pre-compute them using build_gaussians to save time when testing parameters. Small datasets or small gold-standard sets can cause unstable precision curves at the top of the ranked list. Proteins that cannot be fit by a mixture of Gaussians with an r2 above the threshold (default 0.5) are excluded from interaction prediction by default.

workflows.name: predict_interactions_workflow
workflows.intent: Predict binary protein-protein interactions from co-elution proteomics data using a machine learning classifier trained on gold-standard complexes.
input: co_elution_matrix.csv (matrix of protein quantitations across fractions)
workflows.stages: 1. Fit Gaussian mixture models to elution profiles using build_gaussians. 2. Calculate pairwise features using calculate_features. 3. Predict interactions using predict_interactions or the end-to-end PrInCE function. 4. Filter the predicted interactions at a user-defined precision threshold using threshold_precision.
workflows.code:
# set the seed to ensure reproducible output
set.seed(0)
# one-step analysis
interactions <- PrInCE(scott, gold_standard,
                       gaussians = scott_gaussians, 
                       cv_folds = 3,
                       verbose = TRUE)
head(interactions, 50)

precision <- interactions$precision[1:10000]
plot(precision)

network <- threshold_precision(interactions, threshold = 0.5)
nrow(network)

# Alternative step-by-step analysis
data(scott)
# set the seed to ensure reproducible output
set.seed(0)
# fit Gaussians
gauss <- build_gaussians(scott[seq_len(500), ], 
                         min_points = 10, min_consecutive = 5, 
                         max_gaussians = 3, min_R_squared = 0.75,
                         max_iterations = 10)
# filter profiles that were not fit
scott <- scott[names(gauss), ]

feat <- calculate_features(scott, gauss, euclidean_distance = FALSE)
head(feat)

data(gold_standard)
reference <- adjacency_matrix_from_list(gold_standard)
# set the seed to ensure reproducible output
set.seed(0)
# predict interactions
ppi <- predict_interactions(feat, reference, classifier = "SVM",
                            models = 1, cv_folds = 3)

precision <- ppi$precision[seq_len(2e4)]
plot(precision)

net <- threshold_precision(ppi, threshold = 0.7)
nrow(net)

workflows.name: detect_complexes_workflow
workflows.intent: Identify known protein complexes that show statistically significant co-elution in a proteomics dataset using a permutation-based approach.
input: co_elution_matrix.csv (matrix of protein quantitations across fractions)
workflows.stages: 1. Filter low-information chromatograms using filter_profiles. 2. Clean and smooth chromatograms using clean_profiles. 3. Calculate statistical significance of complex co-elution using detect_complexes.
workflows.code:
# analyze cleaned profiles
data(scott)
filtered = filter_profiles(scott)
chromatograms = clean_profiles(filtered)

# detect significantly co-eluting complexes
set.seed(0)
z_scores = detect_complexes(chromatograms, gold_standard)

# remove complexes that could not be analyzed
z_scores = na.omit(z_scores)
# how many could be tested?
length(z_scores)
# how many were significant at uncorrected, two-tailed p < 0.05?
sum(z_scores > 1.96)
# print the top complexes
head(sort(z_scores, decreasing = TRUE))
